question: Which of the following is the longest river in the Peninsular region of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Godavari** is the longest river in the Peninsular region of India.
 
• It originates from the **Trimbak** in the Nashik District of Maharashtra.
 
• The Godavari river flows through the states of **Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha** before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The total length of the Godavari river is approximately **1,465 kilometers**, making it the second-longest river in India after the Ganges.
 
• It is often referred to as the **"Dakshina Ganga" or "Ganga of the South"** due to its significant role in the peninsular region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Godavari** has a number of tributaries, including the **Pravara, Purna, Manjira, Penganga, and Indravati**.
 
• The river basin is known for its rich and fertile soil, making it an important agricultural region.
 
• Several important cities are located along the Godavari, including **Nashik, Nanded, and Rajahmundry**.
 
• The river supports a diverse ecosystem and is home to many species of fish and other aquatic life.
 
• Numerous dams and irrigation projects have been constructed on the Godavari to support agriculture and provide water to the surrounding regions.
